intent.raw_query: Japan family with kids, $4500, cherry blossom season 2026, 10 days from NYC

selected_hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the magical hanami (flower viewing) tradition under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree. Join locals for picnics beneath thousands of blooming sakura trees in a festive atmosphere. Rent a picnic mat and grab bento boxes from nearby stalls for an authentic family experience.
experiences.best_time_of_day: late afternoon into evening for illuminated night viewing

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Explore Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, founded in 628 AD. Walk the vibrant Nakamise shopping street leading to the temple, sampling traditional street foods like ningyo-yaki (sweet cakes) and age-manju (fried buns). Kids love the fortune-telling omikuji slips and the dramatic Kaminarimon Thunder Gate.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: A profoundly moving and educational experience for families, this UNESCO World Heritage site preserves the history of the 1945 atomic bombing. Walk through the Peace Memorial Park, view the iconic A-Bomb Dome, and visit the museum to understand the importance of peace. The Children's Peace Monument with thousands of paper cranes is especially impactful for young visitors.
experiences.location: Peace Memorial Park, Naka Ward, Hiroshima

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Japan's legendary food culture at the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, matcha sweets, and wagyu beef skewers from dozens of stalls. A self-guided family food crawl that introduces everyone to authentic Japanese flavors in a lively, accessible setting.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Togetsukyo Bridge
experiences.description: Wander through the ethereal towering bamboo groves of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most iconic landscapes. Extend the experience with a family rickshaw ride through the scenic area, visit the nearby Tenryu-ji Zen garden (a UNESCO World Heritage site), and stroll across the historic Togetsukyo Bridge with stunning mountain and river views. Cherry blossoms frame the area beautifully in spring.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Kansai International Airport at 13:00. Take the affordable Haruka Express or highway bus to Kyoto Station (approx. ¥1,800–¥2,500). Check in to your boutique stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district. Take a gentle stroll through Maruyama Park itself — Japan's most famous hanami (cherry blossom viewing) park. With late April timing, you may still catch late-blooming Yaezakura (double-petaled cherry blossoms). Enjoy the relaxed atmosphere, local families picnicking, and the iconic weeping cherry tree at the park's center.
day_by_day.evening: Walk five minutes into the Gion district for an evening stroll along Hanamikoji Street — the most atmospheric lantern-lit geisha district in Japan. Watch for maiko (apprentice geisha) heading to evening engagements. End the night with a quiet walk along the Shirakawa Canal, beautifully lit after dark.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: Grab a bento box or onigiri from a convenience store (7-Eleven, Lawson, or FamilyMart) at the airport or Kyoto Station — filling and delicious for ¥300–¥600
meals.dinner: Omen Noodles on Ninen-zaka path near Gion — a beloved local udon restaurant with rustic charm. Budget around ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person. Alternatively, try a bowl of ramen at Kyoto Ramen Koji on the 10th floor of Kyoto Station for ¥900–¥1,200.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase an IC card (Suica or ICOCA) at Kansai Airport or Kyoto Station for seamless travel on buses, subways, and trains. Load ¥3,000–¥5,000 to start. Keep your first evening light — jet lag will be real after a long international flight.

day_by_day.morning: Start early with a visit to Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine — one of Japan's most iconic sites and completely FREE to enter. The thousands of vermillion torii gates winding up the forested mountain are breathtaking. Arrive by 8:00 AM to beat the crowds. Hike at least to the Yotsutsuji intersection (about 30–40 minutes up) for panoramic views over Kyoto. The full hike to the summit takes 2–3 hours for dedicated hikers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back toward central Kyoto and visit Tofuku-ji Temple (¥500 admission). Its Zen garden is stunning and the maple and cherry tree corridors are beautiful in spring. Nearby, explore the charming Fushimi sake district if time allows — Fushimi is one of Japan's top sake-brewing towns with free outdoor areas to wander.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion area. Visit Yasaka Shrine (FREE, open 24 hours) adjacent to your hotel in Maruyama Park — beautifully lit in the evening. Browse the covered Nishiki Market if still open (closes around 18:00) for street snacks.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near the hotel (onigiri, tamagoyaki, green tea) — ¥400–¥600. Or try a traditional Japanese breakfast set at a local kissaten (coffee shop) for ¥500–¥800.
meals.lunch: Inari sushi (fox-shaped tofu pockets with rice) sold by street vendors near Fushimi Inari — the local specialty and very affordable at ¥200–¥400 for a set. Perfect thematic lunch at the fox shrine!
meals.dinner: Hirano-ya near Maruyama Park — a historic tofu cuisine restaurant offering budget-friendly tofu set meals (yudofu) from ¥1,200. Alternatively, grab yakitori skewers from street stalls near Yasaka Shrine for ¥100–¥200 per skewer.

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is reachable by JR Nara Line from Kyoto Station (2 stops, ¥150) or by city bus. Wear comfortable walking shoes — the mountain path is uneven. The earlier you go, the more magical and crowd-free the experience.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Higashiyama Historic District on foot — a beautifully preserved network of stone-paved lanes lined with traditional machiya townhouses, temples, and craft shops. Walk the Ninen-zaka and Sannen-zaka slopes (FREE to walk). Visit Kiyomizudera Temple (¥500 admission) — one of Japan's most celebrated wooden temples built on a hillside with sweeping city views. The main stage juts out dramatically over the forested valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue south through Higashiyama to Kodai-ji Temple (¥600) — a serene Zen temple with gorgeous moss gardens, bamboo groves, and tea ceremony culture. Then walk to Chion-in Temple (FREE outer grounds, ¥500 for inner gardens) — one of Japan's largest and most impressive Buddhist temple complexes, just minutes from your hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Evening free time in Gion. Consider joining a free self-guided Gion walking tour using a downloaded map. Visit Kennin-ji Temple (¥600) if it has evening hours, or simply enjoy the atmospheric streets of Gion as locals wind down their day.

meals.breakfast: Try a traditional Japanese breakfast at Café Bibliotic Hello! in Kyoto — cozy atmosphere, reasonable prices around ¥700–¥1,000.
meals.lunch: Street food along Ninen-zaka: matcha soft-serve ice cream (¥400), yatsuhashi (sweet cinnamon mochi, ¥200), and a savory crepe or rice cracker snack. Budget ¥800–¥1,200 total for a fun street-food lunch.
meals.dinner: Menami Restaurant near Gion for affordable kaiseki-style set meals from ¥1,500. Or try Gyoza Hohei near Shijo for famous Kyoto-style gyoza dumplings — filling meal for ¥800–¥1,200.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday means more crowds at popular sites. Arrive at Kiyomizudera before 9:00 AM for the best experience. Wear comfortable shoes — today is very walking-heavy. The Higashiyama area is entirely walkable from your Maruyama Park hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nara (45 minutes from Kyoto by Kintetsu Express train, ¥680 one way). Visit Nara Park where over 1,200 freely roaming sacred deer bow for deer crackers (shika senbei, ¥200 per pack). Walk to Todai-ji Temple (¥600) — home to Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue, an awe-inspiring cultural monument. Explore Kasuga Taisha Grand Shrine (FREE outer grounds) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site with hundreds of stone and bronze lanterns.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Isuien Garden (¥900) — one of Japan's most beautiful traditional gardens with perfectly framed views of Todai-ji and Mt. Wakakusa. Then wander the charming Naramachi district — a preserved merchant quarter with free-entry historical townhouses and artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by early evening. Relax with a walk along the Kamo River — a beloved local gathering spot where couples and families sit along the riverbanks at sunset. Free and quintessentially Kyoto.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel area café before departing for Nara — ¥400–¥700.
meals.lunch: Kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf sushi) — Nara's most famous local food. Try it at Hiraso restaurant near Kintetsu Nara Station for ¥1,000–¥1,500. A uniquely local cultural experience.
meals.dinner: Ramen or soba near Kyoto Station or Shijo area upon return — budget ¥800–¥1,200. Try Kyoto-style white broth ramen (shiro ramen) for a local specialty.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Kintetsu Day Pass (¥1,500) if planning multiple Kintetsu train trips this trip — it covers the Kyoto–Nara route. Nara is very family-friendly — children absolutely love interacting with the deer. Bring hand sanitizer after handling deer crackers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Arashiyama district in western Kyoto. Start at the famous Bamboo Grove of Sagano (FREE) — walk through towering bamboo stalks for a truly otherworldly experience. Best visited early morning (before 8:30 AM) to avoid crowds. Nearby, visit Tenryu-ji Temple and its UNESCO-listed garden (¥500 garden only, ¥800 including temple buildings) — one of Kyoto's finest Zen gardens with a pond reflecting the Arashiyama mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Arashiyama's quieter corners: walk along the Oi River, cross the iconic Togetsukyo Bridge, and explore the free Jojakko-ji Temple hillside path for elevated views over the valley. Visit Okochi Sanso Villa (¥1,000, includes matcha tea) — a hillside villa with extraordinary panoramic gardens once owned by a samurai film star.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion area. Treat the family to a hands-on cultural experience: book a budget-friendly wagashi (Japanese sweet-making) class in Kyoto — many run for ¥2,000–¥3,000 per person and are highly memorable. Alternatively, visit Pontocho Alley — a narrow lantern-lit dining lane running parallel to the Kamo River, perfect for evening exploration.

meals.breakfast: Konbini breakfast or pick up fresh taiyaki (fish-shaped sweet cakes with red bean filling) from a street vendor in Arashiyama — ¥150–¥200 each.
meals.lunch: Tofu cuisine lunch in Arashiyama — the area is famous for yudofu (hot tofu). Try Shigetsu at Tenryu-ji for a beautiful shojin ryori (Buddhist vegetarian meal) set from ¥3,000, or opt for a more casual tofu lunch at nearby restaurants for ¥1,200–¥1,800.
meals.dinner: Pontocho Alley — browse the menus outside restaurants and choose a mid-range option. Look for set dinner menus (teishoku) for ¥1,500–¥2,500. Many restaurants post English menus outside.

day_by_day.notes: Arashiyama is reachable from central Kyoto by city bus (Bus 11 from Shijo-Karasuma, ¥230) or by the scenic Sagano Romantic Train (¥880 one way) — the train ride itself is a beautiful experience through river gorges and is great for families. Book the train in advance during spring.

day_by_day.morning: Explore northern Kyoto: Visit Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion, ¥500) — the iconic gold-leaf-covered Zen temple reflected in its mirror pond is one of Japan's most photographed sites. Arrive early (opens 9:00 AM) to beat tour groups. Then walk or take a short bus to Ryoan-ji Temple (¥600) — home to Japan's most celebrated rock garden, a minimalist masterpiece of 15 rocks arranged in white gravel that has puzzled scholars for centuries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Nishiki Market (FREE to browse) — Kyoto's famous 'Kitchen of Kyoto,' a narrow five-block covered market packed with 100+ stalls selling pickles, fresh tofu, grilled skewers, matcha products, and local delicacies. Perfect for snacking and cultural immersion. Then explore Nijo Castle (¥800) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site with famous 'nightingale floors' that squeak to detect intruders, ornate painted screens, and beautiful gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Free evening in Gion. Consider attending a Gion Corner performance (¥3,150 per person) — a 50-minute showcase of seven traditional Japanese performing arts including tea ceremony, ikebana, koto music, maiko dance, Bunraku puppetry, Kyogen comedy, and gagaku court music. Excellent cultural value.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Inoda Coffee — a legendary Kyoto institution since 1940. Set breakfasts with coffee, toast, eggs, and salad from ¥1,100. A beloved local morning ritual.
meals.lunch: Nishiki Market street food crawl — graze on samples and small purchases: dashimaki tamago (rolled omelette, ¥300), pickled vegetables (¥200), fresh yuba (tofu skin, ¥300), and matcha mochi (¥200). Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 total.
meals.dinner: Yoshikawa Inn tempura restaurant near Nijo Castle — set tempura meals from ¥1,800. Or try Katsukura tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) near Shijo for a satisfying dinner at ¥1,500–¥2,000.

day_by_day.notes: Kinkaku-ji is reachable by Bus 101 or 205 from Kyoto Station (¥230). A combination bus day pass (¥700) is excellent value if planning multiple bus rides. Nijo Castle is particularly interesting for history lovers — audio guides available in English for ¥500.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Osaka (15 minutes from Kyoto by Shinkansen or 30 minutes by Hankyu/JR local train, ¥560–¥1,430). Visit Osaka Castle (¥600 museum entry, grounds FREE) — a magnificent reconstructed castle surrounded by a moat and park. The museum inside details the castle's dramatic history including the Toyotomi clan's battles. Cherry blossoms in the castle park may still be visible in late April.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Dotonbori — Osaka's most famous entertainment district with its neon signs, canal, and incredible street food culture. Visit the free Shinsaibashi shopping arcade. Walk to Kuromon Ichiba Market ('Osaka's Kitchen') — a lively covered market with fresh seafood, wagyu beef, and local specialties perfect for grazing.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Osaka for dinner in Dotonbori before returning to Kyoto. Experience Osaka's legendary food culture — the city's motto is 'kuidaore' (eat until you drop). Return to Kyoto by 21:00.

meals.breakfast: Quick convenience store breakfast before the train — ¥400–¥600.
meals.lunch: Kuromon Market lunch — fresh grilled scallops (¥200 each), tuna sashimi on a stick (¥400), and tamagoyaki (¥200). Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 for a fantastic market lunch.
meals.dinner: Dotonbori food experience: takoyaki octopus balls from Aizuya (¥600 for 8 pieces), okonomiyaki (savory pancake) at Mizuno restaurant from ¥1,200, and kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers) at Daruma from ¥100–¥200 per skewer. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,000 total for a satisfying Osaka food crawl.

day_by_day.notes: For the best value Kyoto–Osaka travel, use the Hankyu Railway (¥410, 40 minutes from Kyoto-Kawaramachi Station) rather than the Shinkansen. Osaka is a fantastic contrast to Kyoto — louder, more modern, and incredibly food-focused. Children will love the energy of Dotonbori.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku no Michi) — a beautiful stone-paved canal-side walkway lined with cherry trees (late-blooming varieties may still be in flower in late April). The 2km path connects Nanzen-ji to Ginkaku-ji and is one of Kyoto's most beloved walks. Visit Nanzen-ji Temple complex (FREE outer grounds, ¥600 for main hall) — a grand Zen complex with a massive sanmon gate and a surprising Roman-style brick aqueduct running through the grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: At the northern end of the Philosopher's Path, visit Ginkaku-ji (Silver Pavilion, ¥500) — a wabi-sabi temple of restrained beauty with a famous sand garden sculpted into a miniature Mt. Fuji. Then explore the Okazaki Museum District — the Kyoto National Museum of Modern Art offers free outdoor areas and rotating exhibitions (¥430–¥900 depending on exhibition).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Gion. Splurge slightly on a kaiseki-inspired dinner to celebrate the trip. Visit Kyoto Gogyo for unique charred black ramen (kogashi ramen) — a Kyoto original at ¥1,200–¥1,500. Then take a final evening walk through Maruyama Park and Yasaka Shrine, beautifully lit at night.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local kissaten (traditional coffee shop) near Gion — morning set with toast, boiled egg, and coffee for ¥600–¥800. A very Japanese morning ritual.
meals.lunch: Obanzai lunch — Kyoto's traditional home-style cuisine served in small dishes. Look for obanzai lunch sets near Okazaki or Heian Shrine area for ¥1,000–¥1,500. Many small restaurants offer all-you-can-eat obanzai buffets for ¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Kyoto Gogyo (Nishiki area) for kogashi ramen — a unique Kyoto specialty with a rich, charred broth unlike anything else in Japan. Budget ¥1,200–¥1,600. Finish with a matcha parfait from a nearby café for ¥700.

day_by_day.notes: The Philosopher's Path is best walked north to south (Ginkaku-ji to Nanzen-ji) to end closer to central Kyoto. Bring a reusable water bottle — there are water fountains along the path. This is one of the most peaceful and photogenic walks in all of Japan.

day_by_day.morning: Optional half-day trip to Uji (30 minutes south of Kyoto by JR Nara Line, ¥240) — Japan's matcha tea capital and a UNESCO World Heritage city. Visit Byodoin Temple (¥600) — an 11th-century temple so beautiful it appears on the 10-yen coin. Stroll through the Uji River area with its historic bridges and riverside scenery. Visit a matcha tea shop for a ceremonial matcha experience (¥500–¥800).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Kyoto for final souvenir shopping. Head to Teramachi and Shinkyogoku shopping arcades near Shijo — budget-friendly covered shopping streets with everything from traditional crafts to modern goods. Buy omiyage (souvenir gifts): yatsuhashi sweets (¥500–¥1,500 per box), Japanese fans (¥500–¥1,500), and tenugui hand towels (¥500–¥1,000). Visit Nishiki Market one final time for last-minute food souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Kyoto. Pack bags for departure tomorrow. Do a final walk through Maruyama Park and Gion to say goodbye to this extraordinary city. Reflect on the journey over a final bowl of ramen or a cup of matcha.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel area — keep it quick as you have an early train to Uji. ¥400–¥600.
meals.lunch: Uji lunch: matcha soba noodles (¥1,000–¥1,400) at a riverside restaurant in Uji — the green tea-infused noodles are a local specialty you can only truly experience here.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Mishima-tei near Teramachi — a historic Kyoto sukiyaki restaurant with set meals from ¥3,000 (a slight splurge for the last night). Or keep it casual with a conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) dinner at Musashi Sushi near Kawaramachi — excellent quality at ¥110–¥165 per plate.

day_by_day.notes: Uji is a wonderful family destination — the history of Byodoin is fascinating and the matcha culture is very accessible. The Uji River area has free public spaces perfect for a relaxed morning. Confirm your departure logistics for Day 10 tonight — check train times to the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of the Maruyama Park boutique stay. Depending on your flight time, take one final morning walk through Gion and Maruyama Park. Visit Yasaka Shrine one last time in the morning light — it's completely different from the evening atmosphere and equally beautiful. Store luggage at Kyoto Station coin lockers (¥400–¥700) if you have time before heading to the airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Kansai International Airport. Take the Haruka Express from Kyoto Station (75 minutes, ¥1,800–¥2,500 with IC card) or a highway bus (¥2,600, 105 minutes). Arrive at the airport with at least 2.5–3 hours before departure. Browse the airport's extensive duty-free and souvenir shops — Kansai Airport has excellent last-minute souvenir options at reasonable prices.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Kansai International Airport. Carry wonderful memories of cherry blossoms, ancient temples, deer parks, bamboo groves, and extraordinary Japanese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Final Japanese convenience store breakfast or a sit-down morning set at a café near the hotel — savor your last Japanese coffee and toast. ¥500–¥800.
meals.lunch: Airport ramen or soba at Kansai Airport's restaurant floor — surprisingly good quality. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500. Or use remaining yen on airport bento boxes for the flight.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining before departure.

day_by_day.notes: Use remaining yen on last-minute souvenirs, airport snacks, or convert back to your home currency (though rates at the airport are less favorable than in the city). Return your IC card at the airport for a refund of remaining balance minus a ¥220 handling fee. Japan has been extraordinary — consider coming back!

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so morning is in-transit. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Haruka Express or JR Shinkansen from the airport to Kyoto Station (approx. 75 min from Kansai Airport or 2.5 hrs from Narita). Check in to your Boutique Stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle Gion Neighborhood Walk — After settling in, take a leisurely stroll through the atmospheric Gion district. Explore Hanamikoji Street with its preserved machiya townhouses, peek into Shirakawa Canal lined with willow trees and early cherry blossoms, and get your bearings around the neighborhood. Visit Yasaka Shrine at the edge of Maruyama Park for a calm first cultural encounter.
day_by_day.evening: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park (Night Hanami) — Head to Maruyama Park just steps from your hotel to witness the iconic illuminated weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura) glowing beautifully after dark. This is one of Kyoto's most magical springtime experiences and is peak season in mid-April.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a bento box at the airport convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) — budget ¥800–¥1,200
meals.lunch: Quick ramen or soba at a Kyoto Station restaurant such as Kyoto Ramen Koji (basement level) — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Tofu kaiseki at Tousuiro near Gion — a Kyoto specialty featuring delicate yudofu (hot tofu) in a traditional setting — budget ¥3,000–¥5,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Purchase an IC card (Suica or ICOCA) at the airport for seamless transport. April 15 is typically peak cherry blossom season in Kyoto — Maruyama Park will be stunning. Book dinner in advance if possible. Jet lag may be a factor — keep Day 1 light.

day_by_day.morning: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park (Daytime Hanami) — Begin your first full day with a proper morning hanami picnic in Maruyama Park. Arrive early to secure a spot under the famous weeping cherry tree before crowds build. Explore the surrounding garden paths and smaller shrines within the park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kiyomizudera Temple & Ninenzaka/Sannenzaka Lanes — Walk uphill from Gion to the iconic Kiyomizudera Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site with sweeping views over Kyoto and cherry blossom-framed rooftops. Descend through the beautifully preserved stone-paved lanes of Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka, lined with traditional craft shops and tea houses.
day_by_day.evening: Gion Geisha District Evening Stroll — Return to Gion at dusk for the best chance of spotting geiko (geisha) and maiko (apprentice geisha) walking to evening appointments along Hanamikoji Street. Visit Yasaka Shrine again for the evening atmosphere and lantern glow.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast at your boutique hotel or a nearby kissaten (coffee shop) — budget ¥800–¥1,500
meals.lunch: Picnic-style hanami lunch — pick up onigiri, tamagoyaki, and matcha sweets from Nishiki Market (a 15-min walk) or a nearby convenience store — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Izakaya dinner at Gion Finlandia or a local Gion izakaya — share yakitori, grilled vegetables, and cold Sapporo beer — budget ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Kiyomizudera charges a ¥500 entrance fee. Wear comfortable walking shoes — the uphill walk is moderate. Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen') is great for snack shopping and a cultural experience in itself. Gion geisha spotting is best between 17:30–19:30.

day_by_day.morning: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Togetsukyo Bridge — Take Bus 11 or the Randen tram from Gion to Arashiyama (approx. 40 min). Arrive early (by 8:00 AM) to experience the ethereal bamboo grove before tour groups arrive. Walk the towering green tunnels of Sagano Bamboo Forest and enjoy the tranquil atmosphere. Cross the scenic Togetsukyo Bridge over the Oi River with mountain and cherry blossom backdrops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tenryuji Temple and Arashiyama Monkey Park — Explore Tenryuji Temple (UNESCO World Heritage), one of Kyoto's finest Zen gardens perfectly framed by cherry blossoms and mountains. Families can then hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park for panoramic views of Kyoto and close encounters with Japanese macaques.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion & Pontocho Alley Dinner — Head back to central Kyoto and explore Pontocho, a narrow atmospheric lantern-lit alley running parallel to the Kamo River. Choose from the many intimate restaurants lining both sides.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry from a local bakery near Gion or your hotel before departing — budget ¥500–¥800
meals.lunch: Yudofu (hot tofu) lunch at Shigetsu restaurant inside Tenryuji temple grounds — a classic Arashiyama experience — budget ¥2,500–¥3,500
meals.dinner: Kaiseki-style dinner at a Pontocho restaurant such as Kichisen Pontocho or a mid-range option like Pontocho Izuju — budget ¥4,000–¥6,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Arashiyama is extremely popular on weekends — arriving before 8:00 AM is strongly recommended. Monkey Park entrance fee is ¥550 per adult, ¥250 for children. Tenryuji entrance is ¥500 (garden only) or ¥800 (temple + garden). Bring yen cash for smaller vendors in Arashiyama.

day_by_day.morning: Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine — Take the JR Nara Line from Kyoto Station to Inari Station (5 min). Hike through the iconic thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up Mt. Inari. Go as early as possible (7:00–8:00 AM) for a peaceful, crowd-free experience. The lower trails take 30–45 min; the full mountain hike is 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nishiki Market & Downtown Kyoto Exploration — Return to central Kyoto and spend the afternoon exploring Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen') for food tastings — pickled vegetables, fresh mochi, grilled skewers, and Japanese sweets. Browse the nearby Teramachi and Shinkyogoku shopping arcades for souvenirs and local goods.
day_by_day.evening: Kamo River Sunset & Pontocho Stroll — Walk along the Kamo River banks at sunset, a beloved local tradition. Watch families and couples picnic along the riverside. Enjoy a relaxed evening exploring Pontocho or the Gion area near your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early morning coffee and onigiri from a convenience store near Inari Station before the shrine hike — budget ¥500–¥800
meals.lunch: Street food lunch at Nishiki Market — try tamagoyaki on a stick, fresh tofu, and matcha soft-serve ice cream — budget ¥1,500–¥2,000
meals.dinner: Okonomiyaki (savory Japanese pancake) dinner at a casual restaurant near Gion — a fun, family-friendly interactive meal — budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is free to enter and open 24 hours. The full hike to the summit and back is approximately 4 km and moderately strenuous — good for families with older children. Wear comfortable shoes. Sunday markets and shopping areas will be busy — expect crowds in Nishiki.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Nara — Take the JR Nara Line from Kyoto Station to Nara (approx. 45 min). Visit Todai-ji Temple, home to Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue (Daibutsu). Walk through Nara Park where over 1,200 free-roaming sacred deer bow for shika senbei (deer crackers) — a magical family experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kasuga Taisha Shrine & Naramachi — Explore the atmospheric Kasuga Taisha Grand Shrine, one of Japan's most important Shinto shrines, with hundreds of bronze and stone lanterns lining its forested paths. Stroll through Naramachi, Nara's historic merchant district with preserved machiya townhouses and craft shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto & Relaxed Gion Evening — Return to Kyoto by early evening. Enjoy a quiet dinner near your hotel in the Gion district, reflecting on the day's history and culture.

meals.breakfast: Japanese set breakfast at your hotel or a kissaten near Gion — budget ¥800–¥1,500
meals.lunch: Kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf sushi) at Hiraso in Nara — a regional specialty — budget ¥1,500–¥2,500
meals.dinner: Kyoto-style obanzai (small dishes) at a local restaurant near Gion such as Obanzai Kyoto Kiyo — budget ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Deer crackers (shika senbei) cost ¥200 per bundle — a highlight for children. Todai-ji entrance is ¥600 per adult, ¥300 for children. Kasuga Taisha is free to enter (inner sanctuary ¥500). A JR Pass or individual tickets (approx. ¥720 each way) cover the Kyoto–Nara journey.

day_by_day.morning: Travel Day: Kyoto to Hiroshima via Shinkansen — Check out of your Kyoto boutique stay and take the Shinkansen (Sakura or Hikari) from Kyoto Station to Hiroshima (approx. 1.5 hours). Check in to a mid-range hotel in central Hiroshima (e.g., Rihga Royal Hotel or ANA Crowne Plaza Hiroshima).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park — Visit the profoundly moving Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Peace Memorial Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Walk past the iconic A-Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome), the Children's Peace Monument, and the Flame of Peace. The museum provides a deeply educational and emotional experience for families — allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Hiroshima Castle & Shukkeien Garden — Visit Hiroshima Castle (rebuilt 1958), a symbol of the city's remarkable resilience and reconstruction. Nearby Shukkeien Garden is a beautiful traditional Japanese garden perfect for a peaceful evening stroll.

meals.breakfast: Grab a bento box at Kyoto Station before boarding the Shinkansen — budget ¥800–¥1,200
meals.lunch: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki at Okonomi-mura (a multi-floor building dedicated entirely to Hiroshima okonomiyaki) — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Oyster dinner at a local Hiroshima restaurant — Hiroshima is Japan's top oyster producer. Try Kakifuku near the Peace Park — budget ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum (¥200 per adult, free for children under 18) is emotionally intense — prepare children sensitively and allow time for reflection. Audio guides are available in English. The A-Bomb Dome is a free outdoor monument. Shukkeien Garden entrance is ¥260 per adult.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Miyajima Island — Take the JR San-yo Line to Miyajimaguchi Station, then a 10-min ferry to Miyajima Island. Visit the iconic Itsukushima Shrine with its famous 'floating' torii gate rising from the sea — one of Japan's most iconic images. Explore the shrine complex and walk the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mt. Misen Hike or Ropeway — Take the Miyajima Ropeway up Mt. Misen for panoramic views of the Seto Inland Sea and surrounding islands. Alternatively, hike the nature trails through ancient cedar forests. Watch the friendly wild deer roaming freely around the island.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hiroshima & Evening at Peace Boulevard — Return to Hiroshima by late afternoon. Take an evening walk along the wide, tree-lined Heiwa Odori (Peace Boulevard) and browse the Hondori covered shopping arcade for souvenirs including Hiroshima's famous momiji manju (maple leaf cakes).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Hiroshima hotel — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.lunch: Grilled oysters and anago (conger eel) rice on Miyajima Island at a waterfront restaurant — budget ¥1,500–¥2,500
meals.dinner: Casual ramen dinner at Hiroshima Ramen Sato or a local izakaya near your hotel — budget ¥1,200–¥2,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Miyajima ferry is covered by JR Pass. Itsukushima Shrine entrance is ¥300 per adult. The torii gate is best photographed at high tide (check tide tables in advance). Ropeway round trip is ¥2,000 per adult, ¥1,000 for children. The island deer are friendly but may steal food — keep bags zipped.

day_by_day.morning: Travel Day: Hiroshima to Tokyo via Shinkansen — Take the Nozomi or Hikari Shinkansen from Hiroshima to Tokyo (approx. 4 hours). Enjoy the scenic journey past Mt. Fuji on clear days (right side of the train heading east). Check in to a mid-range Tokyo hotel (e.g., Shinjuku, Asakusa, or Shibuya area).
day_by_day.afternoon: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street — Head to Asakusa to explore Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, Senso-ji, founded in 628 AD. Walk through the dramatic Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate) and the vibrant Nakamise Shopping Street lined with traditional craft stalls, fans, pottery, and Japanese sweets.
day_by_day.evening: Sumida River Walk & Tokyo Skytree — Stroll along the Sumida River at dusk and admire the illuminated Tokyo Skytree (the world's tallest tower at 634 m). Consider going up to the observation deck for a spectacular night view of Tokyo's sprawling skyline — an unforgettable family experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Hiroshima hotel or grab an ekiben (railway bento) at Hiroshima Station for the Shinkansen journey — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.lunch: Bento box enjoyed on the Shinkansen — a quintessential Japanese travel experience — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Tempura dinner at Asakusa Tempura Daikokuya, a historic restaurant serving Tokyo-style tempura since 1887 — budget ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter and open 24 hours, though the inner hall has specific hours. Nakamise Shopping Street is ideal for souvenir shopping. Tokyo Skytree observation deck tickets: ¥2,100 (lower deck) or ¥3,100 (upper deck) per adult — book online in advance to avoid queues. Sit on the right side of the Shinkansen (seats A/B) for Mt. Fuji views.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — Start the day early (by 8:00 AM) at the legendary Tsukiji Outer Market for a self-guided food tour. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (rolled omelette), fresh seafood skewers, matcha drinks, and Japanese pickles from the bustling vendor stalls. A must-do Tokyo culinary experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hamarikyu Gardens & TeamLab Planets (Toyosu) — Walk to the beautiful Hamarikyu Gardens, a traditional Edo-period garden with a charming teahouse on a tidal pond. Then head to Toyosu for TeamLab Planets, an immersive digital art museum with stunning interactive installations — a spectacular family experience combining art, technology, and nature.
day_by_day.evening: Shibuya Crossing & Shinjuku Evening — Experience the world-famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing at peak evening rush hour — a true Tokyo spectacle. Browse the neon-lit streets of Shinjuku's entertainment district and explore the Golden Gai alley for a unique atmospheric Tokyo evening.

meals.breakfast: Street food breakfast at Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and green tea — budget ¥1,500–¥2,500
meals.lunch: Sushi lunch at a conveyor belt (kaiten) sushi restaurant near Tsukiji or Toyosu — budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person
meals.dinner: Ramen dinner at a renowned Shinjuku ramen shop such as Ichiran or Fuunji — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is best before 10:00 AM when stalls are freshest and least crowded. Hamarikyu Gardens entrance is ¥300 per adult. TeamLab Planets tickets are ¥3,200 per adult, ¥1,000 for children (ages 4–12) — book well in advance online as it sells out. Wear comfortable shoes for a full walking day.

day_by_day.morning: Meiji Jingu Shrine & Yoyogi Park — Begin your final full day at the serene Meiji Jingu Shrine, Tokyo's most important Shinto shrine set within 70 hectares of forested parkland — a peaceful, spiritual contrast to the city's energy. Walk the forested gravel paths and pass through the massive wooden torii gates. Stroll into adjacent Yoyogi Park, popular with families and locals on weekends.
day_by_day.afternoon: Harajuku Takeshita Street & Omotesando — Explore the colorful, quirky Takeshita Street in Harajuku for unique fashion, crepes, and Japanese pop culture — a fun family experience. Then walk along the elegant, tree-lined Omotesando Avenue for upscale shopping, architecture, and a final browse of Japanese design.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Packing — Enjoy a special farewell dinner in Tokyo, celebrating 10 wonderful days in Japan. Return to your hotel to pack and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Japanese breakfast set at a neighborhood kissaten (retro coffee shop) near your hotel — budget ¥800–¥1,200
meals.lunch: Harajuku crepes and street snacks along Takeshita Street — a fun, casual family lunch — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range teppanyaki or shabu-shabu restaurant in Shinjuku or Omotesando — budget ¥4,000–¥6,000 per person for a memorable final meal

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free to enter (inner garden ¥500). The shrine is especially atmospheric in the early morning. Harajuku Takeshita Street is very crowded on weekends — arrive before noon. Confirm your departure flight time and arrange airport transfer in advance — Narita Express (N'EX) or Limousine Bus from Shinjuku are reliable options. Allow 3+ hours before international departure.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the magical hanami (flower viewing) tradition under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree. Join locals for picnics beneath thousands of blooming sakura trees in a festive atmosphere. Rent a picnic mat and grab bento boxes from nearby stalls for an authentic family experience.
experiences.best_time_of_day: late afternoon into evening for illuminated night viewing

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Explore Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, founded in 628 AD. Walk the vibrant Nakamise shopping street leading to the temple, sampling traditional street foods like ningyo-yaki (sweet cakes) and age-manju (fried buns). Kids love the fortune-telling omikuji slips and the dramatic Kaminarimon Thunder Gate.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: A profoundly moving and educational experience for families, this UNESCO World Heritage site preserves the history of the 1945 atomic bombing. Walk through the Peace Memorial Park, view the iconic A-Bomb Dome, and visit the museum to understand the importance of peace. The Children's Peace Monument with thousands of paper cranes is especially impactful for young visitors.
experiences.location: Peace Memorial Park, Naka Ward, Hiroshima

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Japan's legendary food culture at the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, matcha sweets, and wagyu beef skewers from dozens of stalls. A self-guided family food crawl that introduces everyone to authentic Japanese flavors in a lively, accessible setting.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Togetsukyo Bridge
experiences.description: Wander through the ethereal towering bamboo groves of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most iconic landscapes. Extend the experience with a family rickshaw ride through the scenic area, visit the nearby Tenryu-ji Zen garden (a UNESCO World Heritage site), and stroll across the historic Togetsukyo Bridge with stunning mountain and river views. Cherry blossoms frame the area beautifully in spring.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer from the airport to your boutique stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto. Settle in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity prepared by the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park — Step directly from your boutique stay into Kyoto's most beloved hanami destination. Stroll beneath the legendary 'Gion Shidare-zakura' (weeping cherry tree), iconic in full mid-April bloom. Enjoy a private guided walk through the park explaining hanami traditions, followed by a curated bento picnic arranged by the hotel under the blossoms.
day_by_day.evening: Gion District Evening Walk & Kaiseki Dinner — Explore the lantern-lit stone-paved lanes of Hanamikoji Street as maiko and geiko (geisha apprentices) make their evening rounds. Dine at a renowned Gion kaiseki restaurant such as Nakamura or Kikunoi Honten, savoring a multi-course seasonal tasting menu featuring spring ingredients like bamboo shoots and cherry blossom-infused dishes.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport dining before arrival)
meals.lunch: Curated hanami bento picnic under the cherry blossoms in Maruyama Park, arranged by the hotel with local seasonal delicacies
meals.dinner: Kikunoi Honten or Nakamura — Michelin-starred kaiseki in the heart of Gion; reserve the private tatami room for an intimate family experience

day_by_day.notes: Request a room with a park or garden view at check-in. Ask the concierge to pre-book evening kaiseki reservations if not already confirmed — Gion restaurants fill up weeks in advance during cherry blossom season. Jet lag tip: stay awake until at least 21:00 local time.

day_by_day.morning: Fushimi Inari Taisha at Dawn — Rise early for a private guided hike through the thousands of vermillion torii gates of Fushimi Inari Shrine (30-minute taxi from Gion). Arriving before 08:00 ensures the lower trails are peaceful before crowds gather. Climb to the Yotsutsuji intersection for panoramic views of Kyoto bathed in morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nishiki Market & Pontocho Alley Exploration — Return to central Kyoto and explore Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen'), sampling seasonal street foods including yuba (tofu skin), pickled vegetables, and matcha sweets. Afterward, browse the narrow Pontocho Alley, a preserved dining corridor along the Kamo River, ideal for afternoon tea at a riverside teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Kyo-Kaiseki Dinner with Maiko Performance — Book a private maiko dinner experience through your hotel concierge at an ochaya (teahouse) in Gion. Enjoy a curated multi-course meal while a maiko performs traditional ozashiki games and dances — a rare, authentic cultural highlight perfect for families.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast featuring traditional Japanese morning set (grilled fish, miso soup, rice, pickles) or Western options
meals.lunch: Nishiki Market food crawl — sample wagyu skewers, fresh tofu, seasonal mochi, and matcha soft-serve from premium vendors
meals.dinner: Private ochaya maiko dinner experience in Gion — arrange through the hotel concierge at least 2–3 days in advance; expect ¥30,000–¥50,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Fushimi Inari hike — the full loop is 4km with elevation. Families with younger children can stop at the Yotsutsuji viewpoint (halfway) rather than completing the full summit. The maiko dinner is a once-in-a-lifetime experience; confirm dietary restrictions in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove & Togetsukyo Bridge — Private chauffeured transfer to Arashiyama (20 minutes from Gion). Walk through the ethereal towering bamboo grove in the soft morning light — arriving by 08:30 avoids peak crowds. Cross the iconic Togetsukyo Bridge with views of cherry-blossom-draped mountains reflecting in the Oi River. Visit Tenryu-ji Temple's UNESCO-listed garden, one of Japan's finest Zen landscape gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arashiyama Luxury Experiences — Enjoy a private rickshaw (jinrikisha) ride through Arashiyama's scenic paths and hidden lanes. Visit Okochi Sanso Villa, the former residence of a silent film star with extraordinary terraced gardens and panoramic views. Conclude with a traditional matcha and wagashi (Japanese sweets) tea ceremony in the villa's teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Riverside Kaiseki at Arashiyama Kitcho — Dine at Arashiyama Kitcho, one of Japan's most prestigious three-Michelin-starred restaurants, set in a traditional machiya overlooking the Oi River. The spring menu celebrates cherry blossom season with breathtaking seasonal artistry in every course.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast before early departure to Arashiyama
meals.lunch: Yudofu (hot tofu) lunch at Sagano, a renowned Arashiyama restaurant specializing in this Kyoto specialty, with garden views
meals.dinner: Arashiyama Kitcho — three-Michelin-star kaiseki; book months in advance; approximately ¥50,000–¥80,000 per person; private room available

day_by_day.notes: Arashiyama is extremely popular on weekends — the early morning start is essential. Rickshaw rides should be pre-booked through the hotel. Tenryu-ji garden entrance is separate from the temple building; the garden alone is sufficient and stunning. Kitcho reservations must be secured well in advance — hotel concierge assistance is strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion) & Ryoan-ji Zen Garden — Private guided morning tour to Kinkaku-ji, the gold-leaf-covered Zen Buddhist temple reflected in its mirror pond — especially luminous in spring morning light with cherry blossoms framing the scene. Continue to Ryoan-ji Temple to contemplate its world-famous enigmatic rock garden, one of the finest examples of Japanese Zen philosophy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nijo Castle & Kyoto Imperial Palace Park — Explore Nijo Castle (UNESCO World Heritage Site), the opulent 17th-century Tokugawa shogunate residence featuring 'nightingale floors' that chirp underfoot and elaborate painted sliding doors. Stroll through the surrounding Imperial Palace Park, where cherry blossoms line the wide promenades — a perfect family afternoon walk.
day_by_day.evening: Pontocho Riverside Dining & Sake Tasting — Return to Gion for a curated private sake tasting experience at a specialist sake bar in Pontocho, guided by a sake sommelier. Follow with dinner at a premier Pontocho restaurant with terrace seating over the Kamo River, enjoying Kyoto-style cuisine as the city glows at dusk.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel Japanese breakfast set
meals.lunch: Shojin ryori (Buddhist vegetarian cuisine) lunch at Izusen in the Daitoku-ji temple complex — a serene multi-course experience served in a traditional garden setting
meals.dinner: Pontocho riverside restaurant such as Mizai or Hyotei annex — seasonal Kyoto cuisine with river terrace views; ¥20,000–¥35,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Kinkaku-ji opens at 09:00 — arrive right at opening to beat tour groups. Nijo Castle's 'nightingale floors' are a fascinating highlight for children — explain the history of why they were designed as an anti-infiltration security system. Sake tasting can be adjusted to a matcha or craft tea experience for non-drinkers or younger family members.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Nara — Private luxury transfer to Nara (45 minutes from Kyoto). Visit Todai-ji Temple, housing the world's largest bronze Buddha statue, and walk through Nara Park where over 1,200 freely roaming sacred deer bow for deer crackers — an unforgettable family activity. Explore the vermillion Kasuga Taisha Shrine with its hundreds of stone and bronze lanterns lining the forested approach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nara Continued — Isuien Garden & Naramachi — Spend a peaceful afternoon in Isuien Garden, a stunning two-part traditional Japanese garden framing views of Todai-ji. Explore Naramachi, the preserved merchant district with traditional machiya townhouses converted into artisan shops and galleries. Browse for premium crafts including Nara ink, calligraphy brushes, and lacquerware.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto & Gion Nightlife — Return to Kyoto by private transfer in the early evening. Enjoy a leisurely dinner in Gion followed by an evening stroll through the illuminated Shirakawa Canal area, where cherry blossoms are often still beautifully lit at night in mid-April.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast before early Nara departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Yoshikasai or Edosan in Nara — traditional kaiseki or soba featuring locally sourced Yamato ingredients in a refined garden setting
meals.dinner: Gion Hatanaka or similar intimate Gion dining room — refined Kyoto cuisine; optional private room booking for family privacy

day_by_day.notes: Purchase deer crackers (shika senbei) from official vendors only — unauthorized feeding can attract aggressive deer. Children absolutely love the deer interactions but supervise closely as deer can nip. Nara is manageable in a full day; the private transfer allows flexibility in timing. Confirm evening illumination schedule for Shirakawa Canal with hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Shinkansen to Tokyo — Check out of Kyoto boutique stay after a leisurely breakfast. Private transfer to Kyoto Station. Board the Nozomi Shinkansen (bullet train) to Tokyo — a 2 hour 15 minute journey. Arrive at Tokyo Station and transfer to your luxury Tokyo accommodation (recommend The Ritz-Carlton Tokyo, Aman Tokyo, or Park Hyatt Tokyo). Check in and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Senso-ji Temple & Nakamise Shopping Street — Head to Asakusa for an immersive visit to Senso-ji, Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple founded in 628 AD. Walk the vibrant Nakamise Shopping Street lined with traditional craft stalls selling ningyo (dolls), fans, and premium snacks. Explore the surrounding Asakusa district, including Denpoin Garden (often restricted — arrange access through a guide) and the retro Hoppy Street.
day_by_day.evening: Tokyo Skytree Sunset & Sumida River Cruise — Ascend the Tokyo Skytree (634m) for panoramic golden-hour views over Tokyo, with Mt. Fuji visible on clear spring evenings. Descend for a private yakatabune (traditional wooden boat) dinner cruise along the Sumida River, floating past illuminated bridges and the Skytree's reflection in the water.

meals.breakfast: Final Kyoto in-hotel breakfast or bento box arranged by concierge for the Shinkansen journey
meals.lunch: Asakusa Imahan — premium sukiyaki and shabu-shabu using Wagyu beef in a traditional setting steps from Senso-ji
meals.dinner: Private yakatabune dinner cruise on the Sumida River — traditional multi-course Japanese dinner with seasonal dishes; book through hotel concierge; approximately ¥25,000–¥40,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Reserve Shinkansen seats in advance (Green Car or Gran Class for premium comfort). The Nozomi is the fastest option but not covered by the standard JR Pass — confirm ticketing. Tokyo Skytree tickets can be pre-purchased to skip queues. The yakatabune cruise is a uniquely Tokyo experience that combines dining, history, and sightseeing.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — Begin the morning with an early private guided food tour of the legendary Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet egg omelette), premium tuna, sea urchin, and seasonal Japanese street foods. Visit a top-tier sushi counter for a premium omakase breakfast — a bucket-list experience. Explore the market's specialty knife and cookware shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: teamLab Borderless or Planets Digital Art Museum — Experience the world-renowned teamLab immersive digital art installations — a spectacular and joyful experience for all ages. The vast, borderless rooms of living, breathing digital art are mesmerizing for children and adults alike. Book private or priority access through the hotel concierge to avoid peak queues.
day_by_day.evening: Roppongi Hills & Michelin Dinner — Visit the Mori Art Museum atop Roppongi Hills for contemporary art and the Tokyo City View observation deck. Dine at one of Roppongi's Michelin-starred restaurants such as RyuGin (three Michelin stars, contemporary Japanese), Azabu Kadowaki, or Joel Robuchon Tokyo for a world-class evening.

meals.breakfast: Omakase sushi breakfast at Tsukiji — Sushi Dai or Daiwa Sushi (arrive early or pre-book); approximately ¥5,000–¥15,000 per person for a premium set
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Tsukiji market stall or nearby Hamarikyu Gardens teahouse overlooking the tidal pond — bento and matcha
meals.dinner: RyuGin — three-Michelin-star contemporary Japanese cuisine in Roppongi; tasting menu approximately ¥50,000+ per person; advance reservation essential

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is most vibrant between 06:00–10:00 — an early start is rewarded. teamLab venues require advance ticket booking — they often sell out weeks ahead, especially during spring. Confirm which teamLab venue is operating in April 2027 as new locations may have opened. Mori Art Museum has late opening hours (until 22:00 on most days).

day_by_day.morning: Meiji Jingu Shrine & Harajuku — Begin with a serene forested walk to Meiji Jingu, Tokyo's most important Shinto shrine, dedicated to Emperor Meiji and Empress Shoken. The surrounding 70-hectare forest provides a tranquil contrast to the city. Participate in a traditional omamori (charm) purchase ritual. Walk through the Omotesando Keyaki Avenue, Tokyo's most elegant boulevard lined with zelkova trees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Omotesando & Aoyama Luxury Shopping — Explore Omotesando Hills (designed by Tadao Ando) and the surrounding luxury boutiques — Hermès, Louis Vuitton, Prada, and exceptional Japanese designers. Visit the Nezu Museum for a world-class collection of Asian antiquities set in a stunning bamboo garden — a cultural highlight amid the fashion district.
day_by_day.evening: Shibuya Crossing & Rooftop Dinner — Experience the electrifying spectacle of Shibuya Crossing at night — the world's busiest pedestrian intersection — from the Shibuya Sky rooftop observation deck for an aerial perspective. Dine at a premium restaurant in Shibuya or Shinjuku with skyline views, such as Nakamura Tokichi or a teppanyaki counter featuring A5 Wagyu.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at your luxury Tokyo property — full Japanese or Western set
meals.lunch: Omotesando Hills restaurant or Anniversaire Café — elegant French-Japanese fusion lunch in a chic Omotesando setting
meals.dinner: Ukai-tei Omotesando — premier teppanyaki featuring A5 Wagyu beef prepared tableside by master chefs; intimate counter seating; approximately ¥30,000–¥50,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free to enter; the inner garden (Gyoen) has a small admission fee and is worth visiting for its iris garden and teahouse. Nezu Museum garden is particularly beautiful in spring — allow 1.5 hours. Shibuya Sky tickets should be booked in advance online. The Ukai-tei teppanyaki experience is highly theatrical and beloved by families.

day_by_day.morning: Hiroshima Day Trip — Board the Nozomi Shinkansen from Tokyo to Hiroshima (approximately 4 hours). Visit the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park — a profoundly moving and educational UNESCO World Heritage experience. Walk through the Peace Memorial Park, view the preserved A-Bomb Dome, and pay respects at the Children's Peace Monument. A private guide is strongly recommended for contextual depth and to support younger family members through the emotional experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Miyajima Island — Take the JR ferry to Miyajima Island (Itsukushima), one of Japan's Three Views. See the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine at high or low tide (check tide tables in advance). Walk through the island's forested hills, encounter freely roaming deer, and sample Hiroshima's famous momiji manju (maple leaf-shaped cakes). Optional: cable car to Mt. Misen for panoramic views of the Seto Inland Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo & Dinner — Board the Shinkansen back to Tokyo (arriving approximately 21:00–22:00 depending on departure time). Light dinner at the hotel or a premium ramen counter near the hotel for a relaxed final evening.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast before early Shinkansen departure (depart by 07:00–08:00 from Tokyo)
meals.lunch: Hiroshima okonomiyaki lunch at Micchan or Hassho — Hiroshima's signature layered savory pancake is a must-try culinary experience distinct from Osaka-style
meals.dinner: In-hotel dining or Fuunji / Ichiran premium ramen — a comforting, iconic Japanese late-night meal after a long travel day

day_by_day.notes: This is a long but deeply rewarding day — depart Tokyo by 07:30 to maximize time at both Hiroshima and Miyajima. The Peace Museum is emotionally intense; prepare children with age-appropriate context beforehand and allow space for reflection. Check Miyajima tide times in advance — the floating torii is most dramatic at high tide. A private guide for Hiroshima is highly recommended and transformative.

day_by_day.morning: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden — Spend a peaceful final morning in Tokyo's most beautiful garden, Shinjuku Gyoen — a blend of French formal, English landscape, and Japanese traditional garden styles. In mid-to-late April, late-blooming cherry varieties (such as Ichiyo and Fugenzo) may still be flowering, offering a gentle farewell to the cherry blossom season. Enjoy a private guided garden walk and tea ceremony in the traditional teahouse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Akihabara & Ginza Farewell Shopping — Explore Akihabara's vibrant electronics and anime culture district for unique Japanese souvenirs and technology. Transfer to Ginza — Tokyo's most prestigious shopping district — for final luxury purchases at Mitsukoshi or Matsuya department stores, including premium Japanese crafts, lacquerware, ceramics, and confections. Visit Itoya stationery store for exquisite Japanese paper goods.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Omakase Dinner — Conclude the journey with a transcendent omakase sushi dinner at one of Tokyo's legendary sushi counters such as Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten, Saito, or Sushi Yoshitake. Each course of hand-pressed nigiri by a master chef is a fitting culinary farewell to Japan. Transfer to hotel for final night's rest before departure.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely in-hotel breakfast — savor the final morning without rushing
meals.lunch: Ginza Kojyu or Ginza Kyubey — elegant Ginza lunch; Kyubey is a historic sushi institution ideal for a refined midday meal with family
meals.dinner: Omakase sushi farewell dinner — Sukiyabashi Jiro (Honten or Roppongi branch), Sushi Yoshitake, or Harutaka; approximately ¥40,000–¥80,000 per person; reservation essential and often requires hotel concierge introduction

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen opens at 09:00 and charges a small admission fee — arrive early for peaceful enjoyment before weekend crowds. Confirm cherry blossom status with the hotel concierge — late-blooming varieties often extend the season into late April. Pack premium purchases carefully; most luxury department stores offer complimentary gift wrapping and international shipping. Confirm departure logistics and airport transfer with hotel concierge the evening before.
